concept.title: Fail-closed filtering
concept.shortdesc: When is unsure whether a reader may see something, it hides it. A mistake in a condition can hide content, but never leak it.

conbody.p: For readers, each of these excludes the content it is on:

ul.li: a product or feature value the reader's organization does not hold;
a value that is not declared in opend.config.yaml, such as a typo like product="embd", because no reader can hold it;
a release token that does not parse, such as release="next";
any release condition, when the reader's own version does not parse.

conbody.p: Because a typo silently hides content, validation reports undeclared values (undeclared-value) and bad ranges (invalid-release) as errors, and the hosted build refuses to publish them. You find out in the previewer or in CI, before readers do.

section.title: Lookups fall back, they don't reveal
section.p: The same rule holds wherever content is looked up rather than browsed:

ul.li: A link to a topic the reader cannot see renders as its authored text, without the target's title.
A context-sensitive help key whose topic is hidden falls back to a parent key or the app's default, never to the hidden topic.
An image is served only when a topic visible to that reader references it.
A PDF publication with nothing visible returns the same 404 as one that does not exist.

section.title: Build attributes are different
section.p: audience, platform, otherprops, props and deliveryTarget follow DITAVAL rules at build time instead: a value with no rule is included. Declare them anyway; validation still reports undeclared ones.
